name: Gini Coefficient (Two-Segment Lorenz)
description: Approximates the Gini coefficient of inequality from a Lorenz curve modeled as two straight segments through two kink points. The result is one minus twice the area under the piecewise-linear Lorenz curve, ranging from 0 (perfect equality) toward 1 (maximal inequality).
notes: This is a two-segment trapezoidal approximation, not the exact Gini; more kink points give better accuracy. Population and income shares must be cumulative, ordered, and lie between 0 and 1 with x1 < x2.

name: Poverty Gap Index
description: Gives the average shortfall below the poverty line as a share of the line, counting the non-poor as zero (Foster–Greer–Thorbecke with α = 1).
notes: Times the poverty line and population, it is the minimum cost of ending poverty with perfect targeting.

name: Foster–Greer–Thorbecke Poverty Index
description: Generalises poverty measures: α = 0 gives the headcount ratio, α = 1 the poverty gap, α = 2 the squared gap that stresses the poorest.
notes: Used by the World Bank and national statistics offices.

name: Age Dependency Ratio
description: Gives the number of children and older people per 100 people of working age.
notes: Ageing societies see the old-age part rise sharply.

name: Palma Ratio
description: Computes the Palma ratio, the income share of the richest 10 % divided by that of the poorest 40 %.
notes: Proposed by José Gabriel Palma (2011); it focuses on the tails, where most change in inequality occurs.

name: S80/S20 Income Quintile Share Ratio
description: Computes the ratio of the income received by the richest fifth of the population to that of the poorest fifth.
notes: An official inequality indicator in the EU. Total incomes of the two groups can be used instead of shares.

name: Mean Log Deviation (Theil L Index)
description: Computes the mean log deviation of a list of incomes, an inequality index that is most sensitive to the bottom of the distribution.
notes: All incomes must be positive. It is 0 when everyone has the same income.

name: Generalised Entropy Index GE(α)
description: Computes the generalised entropy inequality index; a larger α gives more weight to the top of the distribution.
notes: α must not be 0 or 1 (those limits are the mean log deviation and the Theil index). GE(2) is half the squared coefficient of variation.

name: Hoover Index
description: Computes the Hoover (Robin Hood) index, the share of total income that would have to be moved to make every group's share match its share of the population.
notes: Both lists must have the same length and order. 0 means perfect equality.

name: Sen Poverty Index
description: Computes Amartya Sen's (1976) poverty index from the share of people who are poor, their average shortfall and the inequality among them.
notes: The income-gap ratio is the average shortfall of the poor as a fraction of the poverty line.

name: Income-Gap Ratio
description: Computes the income-gap ratio, the average shortfall of the poor below the poverty line as a fraction of the line.
notes: Only people below the line are averaged. Multiplied by the headcount ratio it gives the poverty gap index.

name: Old-Age Dependency Ratio
description: Computes the number of people aged 65 and over per 100 people of working age (15 to 64).
notes: Age limits differ between sources; some use 20 to 64 for working age.

name: Gross Reproduction Rate

variables.label: Share of births that are female

description: Computes the gross reproduction rate, the average number of daughters a woman would have at current fertility rates, ignoring mortality.
notes: It is the total fertility rate times the share of female births (about 0.488 for 105 boys per 100 girls).

name: Net Reproduction Rate

variables.label: Survival factor for each age group
Share of births that are female

description: Computes the net reproduction rate, the average number of daughters a newborn girl will have at current fertility and mortality rates.
notes: The survival values are life-table person-years (nLx) divided by the radix and by 5. A value of 1 means replacement level.
